ACCOUNT_DUE_FOR_ROTATION.summary: A venue account has been active longer than its rotation period.
firstSteps: Register and activate a replacement.
Drain this one.
Relaunch the sessions bound to it.

ACCOUNT_READY_TO_RETIRE.summary: A draining account is empty and can be retired.
firstSteps: Withdraw any dust to a fresh address.
Retire it on Treasury.
Delete its secrets.

AGENT_EXITED.summary: Part of a running session has stopped; the session is no longer whole.
firstSteps: Open the session page to see which agent exited.
If live: check the venue for resting orders.
Stop and relaunch the session.

AGENT_STALLED.summary: A hot-path agent has made no progress for a while.
firstSteps: Open the session page; check which agent and for how long.
Take a thread dump if it's still stuck.
Stop the session if it doesn't recover.

ALLOCATION_EXCEEDS_BALANCE.summary: A venue account's live budgets add up to more than it holds.
firstSteps: Check allocations on Treasury.
Fund the account or lower budgets.
Confirm the alert resolves.

BALANCE_LOW.summary: A venue account is low on available cash.
firstSteps: Check the account on Treasury.
Deposit, or move budget to another account.
Record the transfer.

BOOK_RESYNCS.summary: A gateway keeps finding its order book inconsistent and resyncing.
firstSteps: Check the session's logs for MARKET_DATA_GAP.
Check the venue's status.
Stop the session if it keeps happening.
Open the alarm from the alert.
Read the service's runbook.
It resolves when the alarm returns to OK.

COLLECTION_BUDGET.summary: Streams can't be placed because the source's market-data accounts have no connections left.
firstSteps: The alert key is `COLLECTION_BUDGET:<source>`; the `unplaced` label counts the streams.
Open Market Data → Credentials and check the source's market-data accounts (ACTIVE, connection budget).
Decide whether to add an account or collect fewer streams.

COLLECTOR_SHARD_DOWN.summary: A market-data collection shard has had no healthy task for 5 minutes.
firstSteps: Open the shard on the controller's Market Data → Shards page (its id is in the alert key, `COLLECTOR_SHARD_DOWN:<shard>`).
Read its task logs there, or `/collection/shards-<region>` in CloudWatch.
Check the ECS service `shard-<shard>` in `CollectionCluster-<region>` for stopped-task reasons.

COST_ANOMALY.summary: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection saw a service's spend jump well above its usual pattern.
firstSteps: Open the anomaly from the alert's link and read its root causes.
Check whether the named service is still spending at that rate.

COST_BUDGET.summary: The account's AWS spend this month is near, over, or forecast to pass its budget.
firstSteps: Open Cost Explorer for this account, grouped by service, for this month.
Find what grew, and whether something is still running that shouldn't be.

CUSTOM.summary: A strategy or service raised its own alert.
firstSteps: Read the alert's text: the producer says what's wrong.
Check the session page if it names one.
Ask the strategy's owner if unclear.

DISK_LOW.summary: The session's disk is nearly full; the session crashes when the journal can't start its next segment.
firstSteps: Check for a JOURNAL_BACKLOG on the same session; it's the usual cause.
Stop the session before the disk fills.

DRAINING_EXPOSURE.summary: A strategy holds a listing on a draining account while trading it on another.
firstSteps: Check the strategy's positions per account on Treasury.
Decide whether to unwind the old position.
Retire the old account once flat.

EXCHANGE_HALT.summary: All trading on one exchange is halted.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.

FAILED.summary: A session died without a stop request.
firstSteps: Read the failure reason on the alert or session page.
If live: check the venue for resting orders.
Fix the cause before relaunching.

FATAL_ERROR.summary: A session hit an unrecoverable error and is exiting.
firstSteps: Read the error in the alert.
If live: check the venue for resting orders.
Fix the cause before relaunching.

FEE_MISMATCH.summary: A venue charged different fees than the schedule the registry holds for the listing.
firstSteps: Open the listing in Security Master and check its Fees timeline.
Compare with the venue's published fees for that market.
Record the venue's new schedule, or fix the listing's fee group or event.

FEE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED.summary: A venue's API changed the fees of some fee groups (Kalshi series, Polymarket International fee types).
firstSteps: Read the finding's detail for the groups, dates and rates.
Check any "dated from when first seen" entry against the venue's announcements.

FEE_SCHEDULE_MISSING.summary: A live fill landed where the registry knows no fee schedule for its listing.
firstSteps: Open the listing in Security Master and check its Fees timeline.
Record the venue's schedule for that time.

FEE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.summary: Kalshi charges a series or event a fee type no fee schedule can express, so its fees fall through to the default.
firstSteps: Look up the series or event's fee type on Kalshi.
Record its real schedule in Security Master → Fees.

GLOBAL_HALT.summary: All trading is halted by a global kill switch.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.

HOST_CPU_HIGH.summary: The session's instance has been close to fully busy, or throttled, for ten minutes.
firstSteps: Open the session page; check busy against steal.
High steal on a t3 instance means it's out of CPU credits.
If orders are slow, stop the session and relaunch on a bigger instance.

HOST_MEMORY_LOW.summary: The session's instance has under 10% of its memory available; the kernel will kill the process if it runs out.
firstSteps: Open the session page; compare process RSS with the JVM heap.
If it keeps falling, stop the session before it's killed.
Relaunch on an instance with more memory.

JOURNAL_BACKLOG.summary: The session's journal segments aren't reaching S3; they wait on the instance's disk.
firstSteps: Read the shipper's log stream ec2/<instance>/journal-shipper in CloudWatch.
Check gnome-journal-shipper is running (systemctl status, over SSM).
Watch disk space; a long backlog ends in DISK_LOW.

LATCHES_DROPPED.summary: The OMS halted something it couldn't record in the registry.
firstSteps: Open the session logs; look for STRATEGY_LATCHED lines.
Turn on matching kill switches by hand.
Stop the session if you can't tell what was halted.

LAUNCH_FAILED.summary: The launcher couldn't launch a session.
firstSteps: Read the refusal reason in the alert.
Fix it (policies, balances, accounts).
Re-trigger the rule if the window hasn't passed.
Nothing to do; this is a record.

LEDGER_FAILING.summary: The session's ledger writes are failing; the OMS halts every strategy in it.
firstSteps: Open the session page; check the ledger health and logs.
Check the registry API and database (/system).
If live: check the venue for resting orders.

LEDGER_FENCED.summary: The ledger refuses this session's writes; the OMS halts every strategy in it.
firstSteps: Open the session page; check the ledger health and logs.
Check the registry API and database (/system).
If live: check the venue for resting orders.

LISTING_HALT.summary: A listing is halted by a kill switch.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.

MARKET_DATA_BAD.summary: A session's book for a listing has been flagged bad data for over a minute, so its OMS refuses new orders there.
firstSteps: Check the session's gateway alerts (RECONNECTING, BOOK_RESYNCS) and the venue's status.
Open the session's logs for ORDER_REJECTED_MARKET_DATA_BAD and the gateway's resync lines.
Check whether the session holds a position or resting orders on the listing.

MARKET_DATA_BAD_HELD.summary: A listing's book has been bad for over five minutes while the session holds a position there; nothing can trade out of it.
firstSteps: Check the position and resting orders on the listing in the controller.
Check the venue's status and whether the market is still trading.
Decide whether to flatten by hand on the venue or wait for the book.

NEEDS_REVIEW.summary: A position lost ledger events; recovery refuses to trade it until it's adjusted.
firstSteps: Compare the position with the venue.
Adjust it on the controller (ledger adjustments).
Confirm the alert resolves.

NO_PRICE.summary: A held position has had no price for over an hour.
firstSteps: Check whether the market is simply quiet.
Check the collector for that venue.
Nothing to do if the market is quiet.

PIPELINE_FAILED.summary: A data or research pipeline run failed.
firstSteps: Open the run on the controller's Research → Pipelines page.
Read its logs.
Re-run it once fixed if trading depends on it.

POLICY_UNBUILDABLE.summary: A risk policy can't be applied, so the session has killed its target in memory.
firstSteps: Find the policy in the session logs ("can't be applied").
Fix its parameters on Risk Policies.
Confirm the alert resolves.

RATE_LIMIT_THROTTLING.summary: A venue account is being rate limited; orders are being refused locally.
firstSteps: Check which account on the session page.
Look for VENUE_RATE_LIMITED in the logs.
Reduce the strategy's order rate or split it across accounts.

RECONNECTING.summary: A gateway has been reconnecting for over a minute.
firstSteps: Check the venue's status page.
Open the session's logs for SOCKET_ lines.
Stop the session if the venue is down for long.

RECON_MISMATCH.summary: A venue account's cash or a position disagrees with the ledger.
firstSteps: Open Treasury → reconciliation for the account.
Compare the venue's balance and positions with the ledger.
Stop strategies on the account if the gap is unexplained.

RECON_STALE.summary: A venue account's balances can't be read; live launches on it are refused.
firstSteps: Read the error on Treasury for the account.
Check its read-only credentials.
Record a manual snapshot if the poller is down.

RISK_STALE.summary: The session can't refresh its risk policies; it refuses new orders.
firstSteps: Check the registry API and database (/system).
Open the session page and its logs.
If it persists, stop the session.

RISK_UNGUARDED.summary: A live session is missing a required risk policy; it refuses every order.
firstSteps: Open Risk Policies and check this strategy's coverage.
Add the missing policy for each traded listing.
Confirm the alert resolves.

SESSIONS_SILENT_MULTIPLE.summary: Several sessions went silent at once; the registry or the heartbeat path is the likely cause.
firstSteps: Check /system → Databases and Services for the registry.
Check the registry API's 5xx rate and RDS status in AWS.
If live sessions are affected, check the venues.

SESSION_EXITED.summary: A strategy ended its own session; a WARNING means it couldn't close everything it held.
firstSteps: INFO needs nothing; it is a record.
On a WARNING, the body lists each listing still held. Check the venue and close or keep them.

SESSION_HALT.summary: A running session is halted by a kill switch.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.
Nothing to do; this is a record.

SETTLEMENT_BLOCKED.summary: A settled market still has an open position.
firstSteps: Read the detail: needs review, held by a session, or not booked.
Act on that cause.
Confirm the sweeper books it.

SETTLEMENT_PENDING.summary: A finished market's result was never recorded, so its position can't settle.
firstSteps: Check the event on the venue for its result.
Check the classifier's settlement loop.
Record the settlement once known.

SHARD_BALANCE_LOW.summary: A Kalshi exchange shard is low on cash.
firstSteps: Check the account's shard balances on Treasury.
Move cash onto that shard on Kalshi.
Confirm the alert resolves.

SHUTDOWN_FAILED.summary: The launcher couldn't stop a session it meant to stop.
firstSteps: Stop the session from the controller.
If that fails, terminate its instance in EC2.
If live: check the venue.

SILENT.summary: A running session stopped sending heartbeats; its process may be dead or hung.
firstSteps: Open the session page; check its instance on /system → Trading fleet.
If live: check the venue for resting orders.
Pull the logs before the instance terminates.

START_STUCK.summary: A session has been launching for 15 minutes without starting.
firstSteps: Open the session page and its instance on /system.
Read the logs for where startup stopped.
Stop it and relaunch.

STOP_STUCK.summary: A session has been stopping for 10 minutes and hasn't finished.
firstSteps: Check its instance on /system → Trading fleet.
Terminate the instance from the EC2 console if it's still running.
If live: check the venue.

STOP_WITHOUT_KILL.summary: A session was stopped but its kill switch couldn't be set.
firstSteps: Check the venue for orders the session left.
Cancel anything left resting.
Check the registry's /risk/halts endpoint.

STRATEGY_EXCHANGE_HALT.summary: A strategy is halted on one exchange.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.

STRATEGY_HALT.summary: A strategy is halted by a kill switch.
firstSteps: Check the reason and who turned it on (By:).
If automatic: confirm the venue has no orders left resting for this scope.
Fix the cause, then disable the kill switch on Risk Policies.

STREAM_NOT_LIVE.summary: Streams a rule wants have not been collected for 10 minutes, in one source and region.
firstSteps: The alert key is `STREAM_NOT_LIVE:<source>:<region>`; its title counts the streams.
Open Market Data → Shards and filter to that source and region; look for streams not LIVE, or none placed.
If a shard is down too, follow COLLECTOR_SHARD_DOWN first.

STREAM_STALE.summary: Collected streams have been stale or quarantined for 5 minutes, in one source and region.
firstSteps: The alert key is `STREAM_STALE:<source>:<region>`; its title counts the streams.
On Market Data → Shards, find the streams in STALE or QUARANTINED and the connections they're on.
Check whether the venue itself is degraded before changing anything.

AlertingMeta.summary: Alerting itself is broken; other alerts may not be reaching anyone.
firstSteps: Open /system → Services and Scheduled jobs for the alerting functions.
Read the alert router and store logs.
Watch trading by hand (the controller overview) until it's fixed.

Bot.summary: A gnome-bot alarm fired: the Slack ops bot may not be answering questions or triaging alerts.
firstSteps: Open the alarm to see which part (work queue, Slack events, worker, answers).
Read the worker's logs (log group `<Stage>-BotStack-WorkerLogs…`) for "Couldn't answer" and the error after it.
Ask the bot something in Slack to see whether it answers now.

Classifier.summary: A classifier alarm fired: a queue backing up, a worker unhealthy, or a venue feed gap.
firstSteps: Open the alarm to see which part.
Check /system → Queues and the worker's ECS logs.
Redrive any DLQ messages once fixed.
Open the alarm to see which part.
Read the function's logs.
Check the controller still loads.

Launcher.summary: A launcher alarm fired: a trigger, launch or shutdown may not have happened.
firstSteps: Open the alarm to see which queue or function.
If it's the Shutdown DLQ: find the session and stop it by hand.
Read the function's logs, then redrive the DLQ.

MarketData.summary: A market-data Lambda failed, or the collection reconciler keeps failing.
firstSteps: Open the alarm to see which function.
Read its CloudWatch logs.
For the reconciler (`MarketData--ReconcilerLambda-…`), check Market Data → Shards still updates.

Pipelines.summary: A gnome-pipelines trigger or status function failed.
firstSteps: Open the alarm to see which function.
Read its logs (gnome-pipelines-trigger or gnome-pipelines-status).
Re-run any scheduled pipeline that didn't start.

Registry.summary: A registry alarm fired: its API, database, or a scheduled job.
firstSteps: Open the alarm and see which part it names.
Check /system → Services, Databases and Scheduled jobs.
Read that function's logs in CloudWatch.
